# CANDIDA KRUSEI

C. krusei is resistant to fluconazole, and often has some degree of resistance to amphotericin. Higher doses of amphotericin are recommended for treatment of C. krusei due to decreased susceptibility.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Duration of therapy is dependent upon location and severity of infection, and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

References:

- Mandell chapter: Candida Species
- Pappas et al. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2016, 62(4)e1-50
- Sanford keyword: Candidiasis, Candidemia or Disseminated
- Up-to-Date article: Treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis in adults
Therapy:
## Preferred treatment

## Inpatient

Micafungin 100-150 mg IV q24h ($$$) [H,DI]
\*150mg q24h for esophageal candidiasis, 100mg q24h for other indications

### Alternative

Voriconazole 6mg/kg IV q12h for 2 doses, then 4mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,H,DI]
<OR>
Voriconazole 400 mg PO q12h for 2 doses, then 200 mg PO q12h ($$) [R,H,DI]

### Alternative

Voriconazole 400 mg PO BID for 2 doses, then 200 mg PO BID ($$) [R,H,DI]

## Outpatient

### Alternative

Voriconazole 400 mg PO BID for 2 doses, then 200 mg PO BID ($$) [R,H,DI]
